Investment Update
▪The Company’s portfolio remains focused on lower -risk, 
income -generating assets, while lending continues to 
serve as the core business. Proceeds from loan 
repayments and bond redemptions in FY2025 were 
reinvested into selected funds to enhance recurring 
returns while waiting for investment opportunities.
▪During the year, the portfolio was rebalanced toward 
more diversified and liquid investments, with reduced 
exposure to higher -volatility assets to strengthen 
stability and preserve performance.
▪Overall, the portfolio continues to deliver stable and 
resilient growth, supported by prudent capital 
allocation and disciplined risk management.

Global Fund Policy & Trends — Q4 2025
Global policy developments significantly influenced 
investment fund flows during Q4 2025.
US Trade & Fiscal Policy
•The return of trade protectionism, including tariffs on several 
countries, increased volatility in global trade -related funds and 
shifted capital toward US value, infrastructure, and AI hardware 
sectors.
Global Monetary Easing
•Major central banks (Fed, ECB) began cutting interest rates, 
renewing investor interest in growth funds and technology 
equities.
.Thailand Fund Policy & Trends — Q4 2025
Thai ESG Fund Policy:
•Introduced to encourage savings through tax incentives and 
promote ESG investment, offering tax deductions of up to THB 
300,000 (separate from the THB 500,000 retirement allowance).
Monetary Policy Impact:
•The Bank of Thailand cut the policy rate by 0.25% in December 
2025 to support economic growth, benefiting bond and REIT 
funds as lower interest rates boosted asset prices.
Other Tax -Saving Funds (RMF / SSF): 
•Continued to play an important role in year -end tax planning, 
with asset managers launching more defensive and global 
healthcare funds to manage market volatility.

CAGR +2.2%▪Asset quality in 2025 is concerning as the NPL ratio rose to 2.79% (+0.09%), 
mainly due to total loans contracting to THB 18.2 trillion. With the NPL stock 
remaining high at THB 0.51 trillion, it appears previous ratio improvements 
were driven by debt management and forbearance rather than actual credit 
recovery.
▪In addition, the rising share of household -related NPLs — increasing from 25.7% 
in 2017 to 33.6% in 2025 — suggests growing vulnerability among retail 
borrowers despite the overall improvement in headline NPL ratios.
▪Housing will still account for the majority of NPL for personal consumption
▪The Bank of Thailand (BOT) cut the policy rate to 1.25% and introduced a 
“Permanent Debt Resolution” program to support vulnerable borrowers, 
alongside Responsible Lending guidelines to convert chronic debt into longer -
